theme: 3 terms on view styling: the drawing surface, the rounded corners, and the setting that cuts off what sticks out

terms.definition: The drawing surface behind every view, where effects like shadows and rounded corners live.
terms.example: Set the shadow on the Layer, not on the view.

terms.definition: The size of the curve that rounds the corners of a layer.
terms.example: A Corner Radius of twelve makes the card look friendly.

terms.definition: A setting that hides any content that goes outside a view's edges.
terms.example: The image still has square corners, so turn on Clips To Bounds.

quizzes.question: What setting hides content that goes outside a view's edges?

video.title: Layer, Corner Radius & Clips To Bounds | Day 104
video.description:
Learn to explain how rounded corners and shadows work together: Layer, Corner Radius & Clips To Bounds, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Layer - The drawing surface behind every view, where effects like shadows and rounded corners live.
Corner Radius - The size of the curve that rounds the corners of a layer.
Clips To Bounds - A setting that hides any content that goes outside a view's edges.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 104 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

Explain Layer, Corner Radius & Clips To Bounds in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.

Layer - The drawing surface behind every view, where effects like shadows and rounded corners live.
한국어: 레이어: 그림자나 둥근 모서리 같은 효과가 적용되는, 모든 뷰 뒤에 있는 그리기 표면

Corner Radius - The size of the curve that rounds the corners of a layer.
한국어: 코너 반경: 레이어의 모서리를 둥글게 만드는 곡선의 크기

Clips To Bounds - A setting that hides any content that goes outside a view's edges.
한국어: 클립스 투 바운즈: 뷰의 가장자리 밖으로 나가는 콘텐츠를 숨기는 설정

landscape.hook: Round corners ate your shadow. Can you explain why in English?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the card has round corners now, but the shadow is gone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Do you use Clips To Bounds?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. I need it to cut the photo at the corners.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's why. Clips To Bounds also cuts the shadow, because the shadow is outside the view.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the shadow is drawn on the Layer, outside the edges?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The Layer draws the shadow outside, and clipping hides it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use two views. The outer one has the shadow, the inner one has the Corner Radius and clipping.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, or the shadow shape looks wrong.
Every view has a Layer behind it.
